mcqs.question: Which of the following crystal structures has the highest coordination number?
mcqs.explanation: The coordination number is the number of nearest neighbour atoms surrounding a given atom. In SC it is 6, in BCC it is 8, in FCC it is 12, and in HCP it is also 12. Among the listed options, FCC (and HCP) have the highest coordination number of 12. Option C is therefore correct; the others have lower values.

mcqs.question: A solid exhibits a very high melting point and is extremely hard. Which lattice type most likely accounts for these properties?

options.A: Simple cubic lattice of a metallic element
options.B: Body‑centred cubic lattice of a transition metal
options.C: Tetrahedral (zinc blende) lattice of a covalent network solid
options.D: Layered lattice of a molecular solid

mcqs.answer: Tetrahedral (zinc blende) lattice of a covalent network solid
mcqs.explanation: Covalent network solids such as diamond or silicon have tetrahedral coordination (CN = 4) but each atom is bonded strongly in three dimensions, giving very high melting points and hardness. Metallic lattices (A, B) have metallic bonding, which is weaker than covalent networks, and molecular solids (D) have the weakest intermolecular forces. Hence option C correctly links lattice structure to the observed properties.

mcqs.question: What is the correct definition of a crystal lattice?

options.A: A single molecule that repeats periodically in space
options.B: A three‑dimensional array of points representing the periodic arrangement of atoms, ions or molecules in a crystal
options.C: The smallest possible particle of a substance that retains its chemical identity
options.D: A two‑dimensional sheet of atoms stacked without any regular pattern

mcqs.answer: A three‑dimensional array of points representing the periodic arrangement of atoms, ions or molecules in a crystal
mcqs.explanation: A crystal lattice is the abstract three‑dimensional framework of points that describes the periodic, regular arrangement of constituent particles in a crystalline solid. Option B captures this definition precisely; the other options describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.question: Which statement best defines a unit cell in a crystal lattice?

options.A: The smallest repeating three‑dimensional portion of the lattice that, when stacked, recreates the entire crystal
options.B: A single atom located at the centre of the crystal
options.C: The outer surface of a crystal specimen
options.D: A two‑dimensional layer of atoms that does not repeat in the third dimension

mcqs.answer: The smallest repeating three‑dimensional portion of the lattice that, when stacked, recreates the entire crystal
mcqs.explanation: A unit cell is the fundamental building block of a crystal lattice; by translating it along the lattice vectors, the whole crystal is generated. Options B, C, and D describe other entities and are incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify primitive and centred unit cells
mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a primitive unit cell from a body‑centred unit cell?

options.A: A primitive cell contains lattice points only at its corners, whereas a body‑centred cell has an additional lattice point at the centre of the cell
options.B: A primitive cell has lattice points at the corners and faces, while a body‑centred cell has points only at the corners
options.C: Both primitive and body‑centred cells have lattice points at the corners and at the centre, but the primitive cell is smaller in volume
options.D: A primitive cell contains an extra lattice point on each edge, whereas a body‑centred cell does not

mcqs.answer: A primitive cell contains lattice points only at its corners, whereas a body‑centred cell has an additional lattice point at the centre of the cell
mcqs.explanation: In a primitive (or simple) unit cell, lattice points exist only at the eight corners. In a body‑centred cubic (BCC) cell, there is one extra lattice point at the centre of the cube in addition to the corner points. Options B, C, and D describe incorrect configurations.

mcqs.question: In a simple cubic lattice each atom touches its nearest neighbours along the cube edges. What is the coordination number of an atom in this lattice?
mcqs.explanation: In a simple cubic (SC) lattice, an atom is directly adjacent to one atom on each of the six faces of the cube (±x, ±y, ±z). Hence the coordination number is 6. The other numbers correspond to BCC (8) and FCC/HCP (12) lattices.

mcqs.question: Why is diamond much harder than graphite even though both are composed of carbon atoms?

options.A: Diamond has a tetrahedral network (3‑D) lattice while graphite has a layered (2‑D) lattice with weak van der Waals forces between layers
options.B: Diamond contains metallic bonds whereas graphite contains ionic bonds
options.C: Both have the same lattice, but diamond atoms are heavier
options.D: Graphite’s lattice is body‑centred cubic, which is softer than the face‑centred cubic lattice of diamond

mcqs.answer: Diamond has a tetrahedral network (3‑D) lattice while graphite has a layered (2‑D) lattice with weak van der Waals forces between layers
mcqs.explanation: Diamond’s carbon atoms are covalently bonded in a three‑dimensional tetrahedral network, giving it exceptional hardness. Graphite’s carbon atoms form strong covalent bonds within layers but the layers are held together only by weak van der Waals forces, making it soft and lubricating. Options B, C, and D are factually incorrect.

mcqs.question: A new solid is synthesized and X‑ray diffraction shows that its constituent atoms are arranged in a regular, repeating three‑dimensional pattern. Which term best describes this arrangement?
mcqs.explanation: A regular, repeating three‑dimensional arrangement of atoms characterises a crystal lattice, which is typical of crystalline solids. An amorphous solid lacks long‑range order, a molecular cluster is a finite group of molecules, and a polymer chain refers to a linear macromolecule. Hence option C is correct.
